optionalDependencies: Vercel builds on linux/x64/glibc. npm records a platform binary in the lockfile only
when it resolves the tree on that platform, so a lockfile refreshed on a developer's
Mac carries the darwin-arm64 binaries and nothing else -- and `npm ci` on the build
machine then installs no binary at all. lightningcss is simply the first to notice,
throwing MODULE_NOT_FOUND out of its native loader while compiling globals.css.
Declaring the linux binaries below forces them into the lockfile without re-resolving
anything else. Each carries os/cpu metadata, so npm skips them on macOS and they cost
local installs nothing. Versions must match the package that owns each binary:
lightningcss is pinned by @tailwindcss/node, oxide by tailwindcss, swc and sharp by
next. Bump each one together with its parent.
